question: to the Commission Irene Montero (The Left) Subject:

The Spanish Government approved Law 4/2023 of 28 February ensuring the real and effective equality of trans people and guaranteeing the rights of LGBTI+ people. Article 50 regulates changes of name and sex in identity documents for foreigners residing in Spain. The nineteenth final provision empowers the government to adopt any provisions necessary to roll out and implement this law, which it must do within one year of its entry into force. In addition, also within one year of entry into force, the government should have, by means of regulations, authorised procedures for the adaptation of documents issued to foreigners. Three years have passed and the government has not made the relevant changes to ensure that foreigners residing in Spain have this right. 1.
Will the Commission require the Spanish Government to implement the law to guarantee fundamental rights to foreign nationals – often citizens of other Member States – residing in Spain?
What action will the Commission take in the case that non-compliance continues?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (11.8.2026) Equality and non-discrimination are founding values of the EU enshrined in the Treaty on European Union, the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union1. National authorities are responsible to determine the conditions and procedures for legal gender recognition, in compliance with fundamental rights and in accordance with their constitution and the obligations arising under international instruments’ obligations. The Commission’s LGBTIQ+ Equality Strategy 2026-20302 aims at fighting discrimination against lesbian, gay, bisexual, trans, intersex and queer (LGBTIQ+) people to build a true Union of Equality. Among other things, it outlines that the Commission will facilitate exchanges of best practices among Member States for legal gender recognition based on selfdetermination. The Commission will continue to closely monitor the situation of LGBTIQ+ people across the EU within the limits of its competences, and to use all the instruments at its disposal to uphold EU law in Member States.
